reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes buying OneCoin packages for tokens while associating the purchase with fourfold investment value, projected price growth, and token interest. It also encourages recruitment through direct-sales and matching bonuses, including a 10% reward tied to bringing in people whose group reaches a €5,500 balance within 30 days. These purchase-linked returns and recruitment incentives present a financial solicitation with unusually favorable benefit claims, although some comparisons, attributed statements, and figures are unverified and one chart labels its values as projections.

citations.quote: Well you buy a package and with it you buy an educational package for all kind of financial matters, whatever it is that goes together. You also have an amount of tokens.
You use those tokens to mine One Coins instead of exchange it without having to do anything It just works automatically
it allows you to make 10-12% interest out of the OneCoin tokens that will come your way
you make as many people contact me as soon as possible with OneCoin to roll it out as the world's cryptocurrency. There is direct sales bonus, fast start bonus, matching bonus.
If you find more people, and within 30 days your group expands to a group that has a total balance of 5,500 euro you will get it to the top with 10%.

opening.argument: Judge the price discussion as a forecast, not a promise. The speaker expressly says nobody knows what comes next, and the chart distinguishes scenarios while disclaiming a financial forecast. The presentation also compares OneCoin with Bitcoin's earlier price movement. Those comparisons may be optimistic, but optimism and a conditional outlook do not establish that the projected gains will occur or that the speaker guarantees them.

citations.quote: Nobody knows what comes next, of course.
You see a chart picture of the development and value

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the projected price and token benefits as unusually favorable solicitation. But its package-and-token quote describes what a purchaser receives; it does not itself guarantee a resale price. Its interest quote states an asserted rate, while the speaker separately qualifies uncertainty about future prices. The chart's scenario disclaimer matters when interpreting the growth claim.

citations.quote: Well you buy a package and with it you buy an educational package for all kind of financial matters, whatever it is that goes together. You also have an amount of tokens.
it allows you to make 10-12% interest out of the OneCoin tokens that will come your way
Nobody knows what comes next, of course.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Uncertainty about future coin prices does not qualify away the purchase-linked income pitch. The presentation says tokens from a purchased package are used to mine automatically, describes the investment becoming four times its value, and claims interest on the resulting tokens. A chart disclaimer about projected growth does not address those separate return claims.

citations.quote: Well you buy a package and with it you buy an educational package for all kind of financial matters, whatever it is that goes together. You also have an amount of tokens.
You use those tokens to mine One Coins instead of exchange it without having to do anything It just works automatically
where in the end it turns into your investment 4 times.
it allows you to make 10-12% interest out of the OneCoin tokens that will come your way

opening.argument: This is framed as a presentation explaining a currency and its operation. It starts by asking what OneCoin is, walks through the history of payment forms and Bitcoin, then explains the package, tokens, mining and exchange sequence. The speaker also identifies financial education as part of the package. A careful reading should distinguish an explanation of how a system says it works from evidence that every described benefit is a deceptive promise.

citations.quote: This is a presentation of OneCoin. What is it and what can you use to benefit from it?
Then came the gold and silver coins, then we got paper money. Then came the credit card and now we have digital money.
Well you buy a package and with it you buy an educational package for all kind of financial matters, whatever it is that goes together. You also have an amount of tokens.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution cites automatic mining and bonus mechanics, but explaining those mechanics is also what a presentation about how OneCoin works would do. The quoted appeal to contact more people explicitly gives its purpose as expanding use of the currency. Those passages show promotion, but they do not by themselves prove that the educational and operational explanation is a pretext.

citations.quote: You use those tokens to mine One Coins instead of exchange it without having to do anything It just works automatically
you make as many people contact me as soon as possible with OneCoin to roll it out as the world's cryptocurrency. There is direct sales bonus, fast start bonus, matching bonus.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The explanatory format does not change what viewers are invited to do. The opening asks how they can benefit; the package supplies tokens for automatic mining; and the presentation offers both a fourfold investment claim and bonuses for bringing in investors. Those are concrete financial incentives, not merely a neutral demonstration of currency technology.

citations.quote: What is it and what can you use to benefit from it?
You use those tokens to mine One Coins instead of exchange it without having to do anything It just works automatically
where in the end it turns into your investment 4 times.
Everyone that you raise up this investment opportunity and invests into you get 10% of the time for them.

opening.argument: The described transaction includes an educational package, with tokens alongside it; the presentation also discusses ways coins could be exchanged. That is evidence of a proposed product and service, not proof from this video that money is taken without delivery. The sales bonuses are openly described as bonuses rather than hidden. The cited material does not show a viewer paying, failing to receive a package or coins, or being denied an exchange. The judge should not infer those outcomes from an aggressive commercial pitch alone.

citations.quote: Well you buy a package and with it you buy an educational package for all kind of financial matters, whatever it is that goes together. You also have an amount of tokens.
The coins are available and can be exchanged either with a debit card, or in exchange for, let's take again US$ or USD$, if you so please.
There is direct sales bonus, fast start bonus, matching bonus.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's €5,500 group example establishes a conditional sales bonus, not an observed loss or failed payout. Its automatic-mining quote describes the proposed function of tokens included with a package. Neither quote verifies that the product fails to work. The video does disclose recruitment incentives, so the judge can evaluate them without assuming an undisclosed mechanism.

citations.quote: If you find more people, and within 30 days your group expands to a group that has a total balance of 5,500 euro you will get it to the top with 10%.
You use those tokens to mine One Coins instead of exchange it without having to do anything It just works automatically

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An observed victim loss is not needed to identify the solicitation in this video. Purchasing a package supplies tokens for automatic mining; the speaker calls fourfold growth the passive side of investing and offers a direct bonus when someone brought in invests. Calling the package educational or disclosing the bonus does not remove the purchase-linked return and recruitment mechanisms.
